messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Severity P1 — service-wide KV cache growth + continuous-batch queue depth spike detected on pool 'dedicated-eu2-gpu-pool' at 2026-03-15T08:04:36Z. 95p latency up, drop in throughput, automatic failover triggered for some requests. Alert ID: INC-1794009876.

lucy (oncall): saw the pager. I’m on it. starting triage. assigning to eng-runtime.

omar (eng-runtime): on call. looking at metrics now — KV cache size jumped from ~120GB to 880GB in 6m for that pool, continuous-batching latency spiked and tokens/sec collapsed. NCCL errors starting at ~08:06.

maria (sre): grabbing logs and node-level telemetry. ping me when you know which nodes.

lucy (oncall): devon, can we get a quick snapshot of GPU mem/PCIe stats for the pool? suspect OOM/paging.

devon (infra): pulling node stats. I see heavy host swap activity and high NVMe write IOPS on 3 nodes: eu2-gpu-07, eu2-gpu-09, eu2-gpu-12. NCCL logs show repeated "NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled system error" on eu2-gpu-09.

omar (eng-runtime): that matches our timeline. I think the KV sharding/partitioning logic mis-assigned hot keys — one shard got 70% of keys causing cache blowup and paging, then NCCL stalls while trying to synchronize cache updates across ranks.

lucy (oncall): customer impact? kevin (cs) stand by for customer list.

kevin (customer-success): quick check: three paying customers had elevated error rates — acme-inc, betahealth, and statlytics. acme-inc sees 5xx for long-running chat sessions. flagging account owners.

maria (sre): immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) disable continuous batching on the affected pool 2) reduce batch_max_size to 8 and batch_max_latency_ms to 20 on that pool 3) throttle incoming requests to dedicated-eu2-gpu-pool with a temporary 30rps ingress cap.

omar (eng-runtime): agree. also quick-fix: flip KV_SHARDING_STRATEGY from "size_based_v2" to "round_robin_fallback" for the pool — that should redistribute partitions evenly and stop the hot-spot. prepping hotfix now.

lucy (oncall): execute mitigation steps. maria, coordinate throttling. devon, take node eu2-gpu-09 out of rotation if NCCL continues during mitigation.

eng-runtime-bot: Deploy request created: runtime/hotfix/kv-shard-fallback @ a3f4d2e. Approving canary to 1 node in eu2-gpu-pool.

omar (eng-runtime): applying env override to pool via console: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/pools/dedicated-eu2-gpu-pool
{
  "overrides": {
    "continuous_batching.enabled": "false",
    "continuous_batching.max_size": "8",
    "continuous_batching.max_latency_ms": "20",
    "kv_sharding.strategy": "round_robin_fallback",
    "ingress.throttle_rps": "30"
  }
}
```

maria (sre): throttling rule applied. ingress for pool reduced to 30 rps.

devon (infra): removed eu2-gpu-09 from LB rotation and started a controlled restart on the node to clear any stuck NCCL handles.

omar (eng-runtime): canary applied to eu2-gpu-07. monitoring canary metrics. initial signs: KV cache growth stopped on that node, batch queue depth decreased.

lucy (oncall): update customers. kevin, please notify acme-inc and betahealth that we have mitigations in place and are rolling a fix; provide ETA 30-45m for full mitigation.

kevin (customer-success): message sent to account owners. prioritized acme-inc. included brief RCA that we saw cache hotspot causing degraded latency and transient errors.

omar (eng-runtime): digging into root cause: recent tensor-parallel KV cache sharding change (rollout a3a7bd9, two weeks ago) changed partition placement heuristic to be "size-aware". Works normally, but with a sudden shift in sequence-length distribution (customers sending much longer prompts), the heuristic picked very large partition sizes for a small subset of ranks. That led to uneven memory pressure and then cross-GPU NCCL stalls when ranks tried to sync KV invalidations.

lucy (oncall): so it's an interaction between distribution shift and new sharding heuristic. can we add guard rails?

omar (eng-runtime): yes — immediate and medium-term: immediate = fall back to round_robin_fallback and add runtime safety to detect >2x shard size skew and auto-fallback. medium-term = add per-shard dynamic rebalancer and telemetry to emit shard skew metrics. I'll open follow-up tickets.

maria (sre): logs from eu2-gpu-12 show kernel pagefault spikes here: 
```
[08:05:40] page_faults/sec  45000
[08:06:12] nvme_write_iops    230k
[08:06:25] nccl_error         NCCL_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_SYM
```
Suggest we mark this incident as "KV cache partitioning induced paging -> NCCL stalls" in the postmortem title.

lucy (oncall): rolling deploy to remaining nodes now? omar, confirm when canary stable.

omar (eng-runtime): canary stable after 5m. rolling to rest of pool in 2 phases to avoid thundering herd. Phase 1: apply env overrides to 50% nodes, monitor 5m. Phase 2: remainder.

eng-runtime-bot: Rollout status: Phase 1 complete (50% nodes). Phase 2 in progress.

maria (sre): monitoring shows 95p latency dropping from 1.8s -> 220ms over 12m for the pool. error rate for acme-inc dropping to normal.

devon (infra): nodes eu2-gpu-09 back in rotation after restart. NVMe IOPS normalized.

lucy (oncall): good. set incident severity to P1 -> in-mitigation and update status. assign postmortem owner to omar.

omar (eng-runtime): taking postmortem. will include reproducible test and mitigation plan plus telemetry for shard skew. I opened ticket: RNF-1023.

kevin (customer-success): customers notified of recovery. any ETA for full rollback of throttles?

omar (eng-runtime): keep throttles for 30m to ensure no re-emergent instability, then ramp to normal over 15m if metrics stay green.

lucy (oncall): final check: create incident summary for execs and affected AEs. Maria, grab node-level forensic logs for 72h. omar, include the hotfix PR (#1482) and canary/rollout artifacts.

maria (sre): archiving logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-1794009876.

omar (eng-runtime): PR: https://git.redwood.ai/runtime/pull/1482 — hotfix a3f4d2e -> fallback strategy + shard-skew detection. Canary metrics and dashboard links attached in PR.

lucy (oncall): thanks team. keeping channel open for 30m of monitoring. will transition to postmortem thread when we have stable metrics. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-1794009876 status updated: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Responders: lucy (oncall), omar (eng-runtime), maria (sre), devon (infra), kevin (customer-success).
